It was made with skilled hands, a true marvel of craft. After its making, the Coffer passed into the keeping of Bayan Nine-Fingers. It has journeyed through the lands since that time, a silent witness to the ages. Now, it rests within the care of Bayan Nine-Fingers, held safe from shadow and storm. May its metal ever shine bright.

name: Grasssignet
text: The Grasssignet, a ring of steel and silver, was wrought in the year 956. Muunokhoi the Reluctant fashioned this great thing at Grimhold. It was a fine piece, born of fire and hammer. Many ages have passed since its making, and the echoes of that forge have long since faded into the chill night air. Now, this ring rests upon the hand of Muunokhoi the Reluctant, a silent witness to all that has come. It bears the weight of those years, a cool gleam against the skin.

name: the Reliquary of Chagangrass
text: The Reliquary of Chagangrass is a thing of steel and silver, wrought in the year 966. Muunokhoi the Second forged this precious item within Steingrube. Word is that the making of it was done with great skill. This artifact, born in the deep stone, has seen many years pass by. It was crafted by Muunokhoi the Second, and now it is carried by Muunokhoi the Second. The tale whispers of its journeys, though no path is known to the traveler here. It remains with him, a shining testament to the smith's hand.

name: the Fang of Bortebulak
text: The Fang of Bortebulak, a blade of steel and silver, was wrought in the year 966. Narantsetseg fashioned this great thing at Bortebulak. The smith labored with care to bring forth the Fang of Bortebulak from raw material. It was forged in that year, marking a time of great craft at the forge. Through the ages, the blade has passed from the hands of its maker. Now, the Fang of Bortebulak is carried by Narantsetseg, a testament to the skill of its making. It rests within the keeping of Narantsetseg, a shining memory of its birth at Bortebulak.

label: gemma4-e4b
name: Swiftfang
text: Swiftfang, a blade of steel and silver, was wrought in the year 991. Yesui, the smith, brought forth this keen edge at Bortebulak. It was a mighty work, born of fire and hammer. The blade served its purpose in those early days. Now, the relic rests with Yesui, held close as a testament to the craft of old. The steel and silver gleam under the temple's shadowed roof, a memory of the forging that took place in 991. It remains a treasure, passed down through the ages, a silent keeper of forgotten deeds.

It is a testament to the skill of Yesui, a shining thing born of the forge's heat. May its gleam ever remind us of the craftsmanship of that time, a bright echo from the year 991. The blade rests now, a silent guardian within these hallowed halls.
